title: Memory, Reframed 回忆
introduction:
《回忆》是我在 2026 年 4 月至 7 月完成的作品，灵感来源于我对母亲的记忆。随着时间的流
逝，很多关于母亲的记忆已经变得模糊，甚至无法记清一些细节。但我依然记得那些记忆带给我
的感受。我想通过这个作品，探索记忆是如何被保存、改变和遗忘的。
展示方式上，我将作品设计成一个类似于迷宫的空间，利用框架和半透明的硫酸纸搭建不同的层
次。观者需要在空间中不断转向、穿行和停留，就像在记忆中寻找那些已经模糊的片段。迷宫中
的不同节点放置了绘画、浸泡在液体中的花朵，以及旧相册等作品。这些不同的作品共同构成了
一个关于母亲、时间与记忆的空间。
创作过程中，我不断观察和描绘花朵，并通过抽象化的方式让花的形态逐渐模糊、重叠。花不再
只是具体的植物，而是成为承载情感与记忆的媒介。这也与我对母亲的记忆相似我知道这些记忆
真实存在，但随着时间的流逝，它们已经很难被完整地还原。
对我来说花像是一种可以表达记忆和回忆的表现方式它会像人一样生长盛开枯萎被保存从我小时
候起我就很喜欢花我会观察花的形态颜色和变化并把它们和身体联系在一起很多时候我也会想起
母亲想起她作为一个女性她经历过的事情我想表达的不只是一个关于母亲的故事而是这些无法被
完整说清楚的记忆它们会生长开放凋谢也会被保存我不断观察和绘画花的形态将它们慢慢变得模
糊重叠就像我对母亲的记忆一样。
我并不想通过这个作品去讲述一个完整的故事，而是希望观者能够通过自己的行走和观看，感受
到记忆的模糊、重叠与变化。我希望通过花朵、绘画和空间，将那些无法清楚描述的情感转化为
可以被感知的体验。
introduction-en:
Memory is a work I made between April and July 2026, inspired by my memories of my mother. As time has passed, many of those memories have become blurred, and some details I can no longer recall. But I still remember how those memories made me feel. Through this work, I want to explore how memory is preserved, how it changes, and how it is forgotten.
For the display, I designed the work as a maze-like space, using frames and translucent tracing paper to build up different layers. Viewers have to keep turning, passing through, and pausing within the space, as if searching memory for fragments that have already blurred. Paintings, 
flowers submerged in liquid, old photo albums, and other works are placed at different points throughout the maze. Together, these works form a space about my mother, time, and memory.
While making the work, I kept observing and drawing flowers, gradually abstracting them so that their forms blurred and overlapped. The flowers are no longer just specific plants; they became a medium that carries emotion and memory. This mirrors my memories of my mother: I know these memories are real, but as time passes, they become harder and harder to piece back together.
To me, flowers are a way of expressing memory and remembering. Like people, they grow, 
bloom, wither, and can be preserved. I have loved flowers since I was a child. I would study 
their forms, colours, and changes, and connect them with the body. I often find myself thinking of my mother, too, and of what she lived through as a woman. What I want to express is not only a story about my mother, but memories that can never be fully put into words. They grow, open, fade, and are also preserved. I keep observing and painting flowers, letting their forms slowly blur and overlap, just like my memories of my mother.
I don’t want this work to tell a complete story. Instead, I hope that by walking through it and looking, viewers can feel how memory blurs, overlaps, and changes. Through flowers, painting, and space, I hope to turn emotions that cannot be clearly described into an experience that can be felt.
